blocks.content: Quiz: What is the purpose of git add before git commit?
Tap an option below to answer:
It uploads files to GitHub so they are backed up before committing
git add works entirely on your local machine. Nothing goes to GitHub until you run git push. The add command is about selecting what goes into the next commit.
git add works entirely on your local machine. Nothing goes to GitHub until you run git push. The add command is about selecting what goes into the next commit.
It checks the files for syntax errors before they are saved
Git has no built-in syntax checking. git add is purely a selection step — it moves files into the staging area so you can choose exactly what goes into the next commit.
Git has no built-in syntax checking. git add is purely a selection step — it moves files into the staging area so you can choose exactly what goes into the next commit.
It selects which changes to include in the next commit by moving them to the staging area
Correct. git add moves changes into the staging area — the holding space for "what will be in this save." The commit then captures everything in the staging area as a permanent snapshot.
Correct. git add moves changes into the staging area — the holding space for "what will be in this save." The commit then captures everything in the staging area as a permanent snapshot.
It creates a backup copy of the file in case the commit fails
Git does not create backup copies with git add. The staging area is a selection mechanism, not a safety copy. Commits are what create the permanent history.
Git does not create backup copies with git add. The staging area is a selection mechanism, not a safety copy. Commits are what create the permanent history.
